text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000214 bills 99215 at roughly 2.5 times the all-provider rate in every complexity stratum, but the few returned charts support the billed levels, so the pattern is not resolved either way.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The by-complexity table shows the 99215 share elevated at every condition count, from 0 conditions to 5+, so a sicker panel does not explain the excess, and the mix also leans heavily on 99214. The documentation does not confirm upcoding: all six documented 99215 claims supported the billed level. Six charts is too thin to rule out inflated notes, though. Several note signals deserve attention: the time-repeat and problem-list flags, the 4 notes claiming moderate-plus data review with no lab or test line on the claim, and the missing audit trail. Claim C0108812 is worth a close look because it is a single-condition hypertension visit documented as high MDM at 50 minutes and also appears among the problem-flagged notes. The reviewer should first request more charts, prioritizing the low-complexity 99215 claims in the packet (for example C0108863, C0109028 and C0109351) and a sample of 99214s, and should obtain the EHR audit trail to check whether these notes are templated or cloned."}
